chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

If a person in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) has a spot of impurity on his garment but is unaware of it, and he prays in it, then later becomes aware of it, he is told: 'He does not repeat [the prayer] if he was not aware.' This does not contradict the interpretation we mentioned, because this report is understood to mean that if he was unaware during the prayer, but had previously known that impurity had occurred on the garment, then it becomes obligatory upon him at that time to repeat the prayer.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if one is unaware of impurity on their clothing during the prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between ignorance of an impurity during prayer versus prior knowledge, establishing that the obligation to repeat the prayer arises only when the impurity was known beforehand. The accompanying commentary explains that this ruling does not contradict the principle of *ta'wil* (interpretation) because the exemption applies specifically to cases where the person remained unaware throughout the prayer act. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the condition of *'ilm* (knowledge) as a prerequisite for the validity of ritual purity in practical worship.
